text: Samacá is a town and municipality located in the Central Boyacá Province within the Colombian Department of Boyacá. It shares borders with Cucaita and Tunja to the east, Ráquira to the west, Sáchica, Sora, and Cucaita to the north, and Ventaquemada, Ráquira, and Guachetá (in Cundinamarca) to the south. The town's original name derives from the Chibcha native language, where "Sa" denotes a noble title, "Ma" is a proper name, and "Cá" means a sovereign enclosure. Before the Spanish conquest of the Muisca, Samacá was a small village situated around a large lagoon known as "Lake of Cansicá" or "Valley of the Lake" (la laguna de Cansicá), surrounded by three native settlements: Patagüy, Foacá, and Sáchica. It was governed by the zaque of Hunza, and the modern town was officially founded on January 1, 1556, by Juan de los Barrios. Key economic activities include farming, cattle rearing, and mining, with primary agricultural products being potatoes, peas, corn, and beets. Coal mining is the dominant industry, and most of the coal produced is exported. Over the past decade, the local economy has experienced significant growth, and Samacá is open to international investment. Its geographic coordinates are 5°30′N 73°29′W (5.500°N 73.483°W).
